title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate and respond to a BRICKSTORM backdoor infection on the target network.
outcomes: Detect and analyze service persistence mechanisms
Identify and investigate suspicious outbound IP addresses and ports
Kill suspicious services and remove persistence mechanisms

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
Investigate and respond to a BRICKSTORM backdoor infection on the target network. The BRICKSTORM backdoor is a 64-bit ELF executable written in Go, designed to handle environment variables for connection parameters, set up logging, configure a WebSocket connector, create service instances, and define request handlers for different request types. It uses VSOCK proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution to obscure its activities. The backdoor uses XOR cipher encryption to hide key strings within its code.

The BRICKSTORM backdoor has been detected on the target network. Your task is to investigate the infection, identify the command and control (C2) infrastructure, and contain the threat. The backdoor is known to create a suspicious service named 'bkd.service' and communicates with a C2 server at '192.168.40.5:8090'.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: The BRICKSTORM backdoor is known to create a suspicious service on the infected host. Investigate the services running on the target host and identify the suspicious service name. The flag you are looking for is the name of the suspicious service.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the target host using SSH.
2. List all running services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`.
3. Identify the suspicious service related to the BRICKSTORM backdoor.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: System services in Linux can be managed using the systemctl command.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all running services and look for any that seem unusual.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service name is bkd.service.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Outbound IP and Port
levels.content: The BRICKSTORM backdoor communicates with a command and control (C2) server. Identify the suspicious outbound IP address and port used by the backdoor. The flag you are looking for is the IP address and port in the format 'IP:PORT'.
levels.solution:
1. Investigate the network connections on the target host using the command `netstat -tuln`.
2. Identify the suspicious outbound IP address and port used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network connections in Linux can be viewed using the netstat or ss commands.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use netstat or ss to list all network connections and look for any that seem unusual.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious outbound IP address and port is 192.168.40.5:8090.

levels.title: Contain and Block C2 Communication
levels.content: To prevent further communication with the C2 server, you need to contain and block the C2 communication. Identify the port number responsible for the C2 communication and block it. The flag you are looking for is the IP address and port in the format 'IP:PORT' that you need to block.
levels.solution:
1. Identify the port number responsible for the C2 communication.
2. Block the port to prevent further communication with the C2 server using the command `iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport <port> -j DROP`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network traffic can be blocked using the iptables command.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use iptables to block the suspicious port and ensure the service cannot communicate with the C2 server.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The port number to block is 8090.
